_readme.context: Every user-facing string in the product UI, one entry per unique string. Object key = stable ID. `original` is the string as first drafted; `translation` is where a tone edit goes. They match — nothing is outstanding. Braces mark runtime values: {album}, {n}; square brackets in login.blurb mark link text. Screens are referred to by number: 01 Log in, 02 Set up playlists, 03 First records, 04 Board, 05 Playing, 06 Album detail, 07 Add albums, 08 Narrow board, 09 Settings. Excluded on purpose: sample data (album/artist/track names, durations, dates, 'joe'), icon glyphs (their aria-labels are here instead), and Spotify scope identifiers (their descriptions are here). Strings that appear on more than one screen are listed once, with every location in the context.

app.name.context: Product name. Top-left of every in-app header next to the G mark; also the login screen heading and the browser title.

login.blurb.context: The only explanatory copy on the login screen, replacing three numbered steps. The bracketed part is a link to the blog post describing the method. Nothing else in the product explains the rules.
login.blurb.original: A kanban visualization tool for [Joe's system for giving records a fair shake by listening to them five times](https://blog.joewoods.dev/music/the-album-gauntlet-over-engineered-music-appreciation/).
login.blurb.translation: A kanban visualization tool for [Joe's system for giving records a fair shake by listening to them five times](https://blog.joewoods.dev/music/the-album-gauntlet-over-engineered-music-appreciation/).

nav.addAlbums.context: Header button, screens 04-09. Also repeated as a full-width ghost button at the bottom of the Queue column on 04 and 08. Opens the add-albums modal.

card.play.aria.context: Screen-reader label for the play button that appears over album art on hover. Every card, every screen.

card.more.aria.context: Screen-reader label for the ⋯ overflow button on a card. Menu contains Play, Move to, Mark done, Abandon, Remove, Open in Spotify.

card.open.aria.context: Screen-reader label for the click target covering the card body, which opens the album drawer. {album} is the album title.

common.close.aria.context: Screen-reader label on the ✕ button and on the scrim behind a modal or drawer. Screens 06 and 07.

column.queue.name.context: Column heading, first column. Also the band label above it, the playlist suffix (Gauntlet · Queue), and the destination named in the add-albums footer.

column.stage.name.context: Heading for the four middle columns, where {n} is 1-4. Rendered with a multiplication sign, not the letter x. Also used as a chip on cards in the narrow board and as a playlist suffix.

column.done.name.context: Column heading, second-to-last. Also a playlist suffix and referenced in several progress strings.

column.abandoned.name.context: Column heading, last. Records dropped on purpose. Also a playlist suffix.

band.inProgress.context: Uppercase band label spanning the four ×N columns, above the column headings. Screens 04-08.

band.finished.context: Uppercase band label spanning Done and Abandoned.

column.x4.empty.context: Empty state inside the ×4 column on the full board. Two lines. Reassures that you never file cards here yourself.

column.empty.short.context: One-word empty state used in abbreviated boards behind a modal or drawer.

board.dropSlot.title.context: Green dashed placeholder shown in a column while dragging a card over it.

board.dropSlot.detail.context: Second line of the drag placeholder, naming what will happen. {album} is the dragged album, {column} the destination.

card.meta.context: Third line on a board card. {year}, {n} track count, {duration} total runtime. Abbreviated because column width is 244px.

card.dots.label.context: Text beside the five progress dots on a card. {n} is completed listens, always out of five.

card.pass.context: Progress row under a card, shown only while a pass is underway. {done} tracks heard so far this pass, {total} on the album. Empties if the listener skips a track.

card.playing.position.context: Replaces the meta line on the card currently playing. Deliberately about position in the album, not the track. {time} is time left in the whole record.

card.done.meta.context: Meta line on cards in the Done column. {date} is when it reached Done, read from the playlist add date.

card.abandoned.meta.context: Meta line on cards in the Abandoned column. {date} is when it was dropped.

card.movedChip.context: Green chip on a card that just advanced a column, alongside the toast. Screen 05.

card.movingChip.context: Chip on a card while a move the listener asked for is being written — dragged into another column, sent there from the card menu or the album drawer, or an advance being undone. {column} is where it is going. Sits where card.movedChip sits, and a spinner sits over the album art beside it. Screens 04, 05, 08.

login.cta.context: The primary button on the login screen. Full width, green.

login.premium.context: Small print under the login button. Two sentences.
login.premium.original: Spotify Premium is required to play inside the app; free accounts can still use the board and open albums in the Spotify app.
login.premium.translation: Spotify Premium is required to play inside the app; free accounts can still use the board and open albums in the Spotify app.

login.footer.storage.context: Footer strip of the login card. The no-database claim, stated where someone is deciding whether to hand over Spotify access.
login.footer.storage.original: We don't track any data about you; everything lives in Spotify.
login.footer.storage.translation: We don't track any data about you; everything lives in Spotify.

login.footer.link.context: Link at the right of the login card footer.

login.scopes.summary.context: Collapsed disclosure toggle below the login card. Expands into the permissions table.
login.scopes.summary.original: What access are we asking for?
login.scopes.summary.translation: What access are we asking for?

login.scope.playlistModify.context: Plain-English reason for the playlist-modify-private scope, in the permissions table.
login.scope.playlistModify.original: Create and reorder the seven board playlists
login.scope.playlistModify.translation: Create and reorder the seven board playlists

login.scope.playlistModifyPublic.context: Plain-English reason for the playlist-modify-public scope, in the permissions table. Only exercised when the Private switch on the setup screen is turned off.
login.scope.playlistModifyPublic.original: Create them as public playlists, if you turn Private off
login.scope.playlistModifyPublic.translation: Create them as public playlists, if you turn Private off

login.scope.playlistRead.context: Plain-English reason for the playlist-read-private scope.
login.scope.playlistRead.original: Read what's on the board, import an existing queue
login.scope.playlistRead.translation: Read what's on the board, import an existing queue

login.scope.readPlayback.context: Plain-English reason for the user-read-playback-state scope.
login.scope.readPlayback.original: Know what's playing and how far in
login.scope.readPlayback.translation: Know what's playing and how far in

login.scope.modifyPlayback.context: Plain-English reason for the user-modify-playback-state scope.
login.scope.modifyPlayback.original: Start an album from a card
login.scope.modifyPlayback.translation: Start an album from a card

login.scope.recentlyPlayed.context: Plain-English reason for the user-read-recently-played scope. This one is load-bearing — it's how progress is reconstructed at all.
login.scope.recentlyPlayed.original: Credit listens that happened outside the app
login.scope.recentlyPlayed.translation: Credit listens that happened outside the app

login.scope.topRead.context: Plain-English reason for the user-top-read scope, which powers screen 03.
login.scope.topRead.original: Work out which records you already know a song from
login.scope.topRead.translation: Work out which records you already know a song from

login.scope.libraryRead.context: Plain-English reason for the user-library-read scope.
login.scope.libraryRead.original: Offer your saved albums when filling the queue
login.scope.libraryRead.translation: Offer your saved albums when filling the queue

login.scope.streaming.context: Plain-English reason for the streaming scope.

login.scope.readPrivate.context: Plain-English reason for the user-read-private scope, in the permissions table. Without it Spotify withholds `product`, and Settings names every account Free.
login.scope.readPrivate.original: Tell a Premium account from a Free one
login.scope.readPrivate.translation: Tell a Premium account from a Free one

setup.title.context: Page heading, screen 02 — shown once, right after login.

setup.playlists.head.context: Heading of the first panel on setup, listing what's about to be created.

setup.playlists.sub.context: Lighter text after the panel heading. {user} is the Spotify display name.

setup.private.label.context: Label on the switch controlling whether the created playlists are private. On by default.

setup.plays.chip.context: Chip at the right of each row in the setup playlist list, showing what that column means numerically. {n} is 0-5. Needs singular '1 play' at n=1; Abandoned shows an em dash instead.

setup.playlists.foot.context: Footer strip of the setup playlist panel. The names are how the app finds the playlists again on each load, since nothing is stored — so renaming one really does orphan that column.
setup.playlists.foot.original: Don't rename these, otherwise you'll lose your place!
setup.playlists.foot.translation: Don't rename these, otherwise you'll lose your place!

setup.learnMore.context: Link below the playlist panel on Setup, replacing a three-rule panel. Points at the same blog post as the login blurb.
setup.learnMore.original: Learn more about The Album Gauntlet
setup.learnMore.translation: Learn more about The Album Gauntlet

setup.cta.primary.context: Primary button at the bottom of setup. Creates the playlists and goes to screen 03.

setup.creating.context: Shown beside the setup button while the seven playlists are being created. A library with hundreds of playlists takes a moment to scan, and a spinner alone says nothing about why.
setup.creating.original: Creating the seven playlists in your library…
setup.creating.translation: Creating the seven playlists in your library…

first.title.context: Page heading, screen 03. The onboarding question, shown once after the playlists are created.

first.panel.head.context: Heading of the suggestions panel on screen 03. Names the signal the list is built from.

first.range.4weeks.context: Segmented control option on screen 03, top right of the panel. Maps to Spotify's short_term window.

first.range.6months.context: Segmented control option on screen 03. Maps to medium_term. Selected by default.

first.range.allTime.context: Segmented control option on screen 03. Maps to long_term.

first.tile.meta.context: Third line on a suggestion tile, screen 03. No runtime: suggestions are grouped out of top tracks, which carry the album but not its track list, so a total would always be 0m.

first.tile.meta.saved.context: Variant of the tile meta line when the album is already in the listener's Spotify library.

first.why.single.context: Green reason line on a suggestion tile when one track from the album is in the listener's top songs. Preceded by a ♪ glyph. {rank} is its position in the list — Spotify gives a ranking, never a play count, so this must not claim a number of plays.

first.why.multi.context: Green reason line when several tracks from the album are in the top songs. {n} is how many. This is the strongest signal and sorts highest.

first.showMore.context: Ghost button below the suggestion grid on screen 03. {n} is how many more are available.

first.filterNote.context: Small grey text beside the Show more button, explaining what's been filtered out of the suggestions.
first.filterNote.original: Singles are left off this list.
first.filterNote.translation: Singles are left off this list.

first.bar.count.context: Running count in the sticky bottom bar of screen 03. Updates as tiles are selected. {playlist} is the Queue playlist name.
first.bar.count.original: {n} records selected · {t} tracks will be added to {playlist}
first.bar.count.translation: {n} records selected · {t} tracks will be added to {playlist}

first.cta.skip.context: Secondary button in the screen 03 action bar. Goes to an empty board.

first.cta.primary.context: Primary button in the screen 03 action bar — the last step of onboarding. Adds the selected albums to Queue and opens the board.

playing.toast.context: Dark toast at the bottom of the board when an album advances. The payoff moment. {album}, {n} is the new listen count as an ordinal, {column} the destination.

playing.toast.undo.context: Green button inside the advance toast. Available for 30 seconds, then gone; lives in the page only, so a reload loses it.

playing.addToQueue.context: Green button at the left of the playback bar, beside the record playing. Adds that record to the Queue column. Shown only while the record is on none of the seven playlists — one already on the board has a card to act on instead, and the playlist model can't hold it in two columns.

playing.shuffle.title.context: Tooltip on the shuffle button in the playback bar, which is disabled whenever a board album is playing. Explains why rather than just greying out.
playing.shuffle.title.original: You can't shuffle here, we're listening to albums cover-to-cover!
playing.shuffle.title.translation: You can't shuffle here, we're listening to albums cover-to-cover!

playing.repeat.title.context: Tooltip on the repeat button in the playback bar. Repeat is allowed and every full pass counts.

playing.prev.aria.context: Screen-reader label, playback bar transport control.

playing.pause.aria.context: Screen-reader label on the main transport button while audio is playing. Becomes 'Play' when paused.

playing.next.aria.context: Screen-reader label, playback bar transport control. Using it ends the current pass.

playing.queueButton.context: Button at the right of the playback bar, preceded by a list glyph. Opens the upcoming-tracks queue.

playing.volume.context: Tiny label before the volume slider in the playback bar. Abbreviated for space.

playing.error.noDevice.context: Alert under the header when starting a record fails because Spotify has no active device. Spotify's own words for this are 'Player command failed: No active device found', which names nothing the listener can do.
playing.error.noDevice.original: Nothing to play on — open Spotify on a phone, computer or speaker, then try again.
playing.error.noDevice.translation: Nothing to play on — open Spotify on a phone, computer or speaker, then try again.

playing.error.premium.context: Same alert, when Spotify refuses playback because the account is Free. The board still works; 'Open in Spotify' is the way out.
playing.error.premium.original: Playing from here needs Spotify Premium. Use Open in Spotify instead.
playing.error.premium.translation: Playing from here needs Spotify Premium. Use Open in Spotify instead.

playing.error.offline.context: Same alert, when the request never reached the server at all.

playing.error.generic.context: Same alert, when Spotify refused the command without saying why. The fallback: better a vague refusal than a button that does nothing.
playing.error.generic.original: Spotify would not start that record.
playing.error.generic.translation: Spotify would not start that record.

playing.error.dismiss.context: Button that closes the playback alert. The alert otherwise stays until the next command works, since an error worth reading should not time out.

album.meta.context: Meta line under the album title in the album drawer, screen 07. Carries a runtime, unlike first.tile.meta, because the drawer has the album's track list to total.

album.drawer.kicker.context: Small grey label at the top of the album drawer, screen 06, before the column chip.

album.drawer.columnChip.context: Green chip at the top of the album drawer showing which column the album is in. {column} is e.g. ×3.

album.play.context: Primary button in the album drawer, preceded by a play glyph. Starts the record from track 1.

album.openSpotify.context: Secondary button in the album drawer. Also what replaces the play button for free accounts.

album.listens.context: Bold sentence beside the five dots in the album drawer. {n} is completed listens.

album.pass.label.context: Left side of the progress row in the album drawer. {n} is which pass this is — pass 4 means three complete listens already banked.

album.pass.count.context: Right side of the album drawer progress row, in monospace.

album.tracks.head.context: Uppercase section heading above the tracklist in the album drawer.

album.sinceLine.context: Single line at the bottom of the album drawer body, above the action buttons. The only history the app can show, since it comes from the playlist add date. {column}, {date}.

album.action.moveTo.context: Button in the album drawer footer, opens a column menu. The keyboard-accessible equivalent of dragging a card.

album.action.markComplete.context: Button in the album drawer footer. Advances the album one column without playback — for a listen on vinyl, another service, or one the history window lost.

album.action.abandon.context: Button in the album drawer footer. Moves the album to Abandoned.

album.action.remove.context: Button in the album drawer footer, styled quietest of the four. Takes the album off the board entirely; the album stays in the listener's library.

add.modal.title.context: Heading of the add-albums modal, screens 07, 07b and 07c. Names the destination column.

add.modal.aria.context: Screen-reader label on the add-albums dialog itself.

add.tab.search.context: Tab in the add-albums modal, selected by default. Searches all of Spotify.

add.tab.saved.context: Tab in the add-albums modal. {n} is the count of saved albums in the listener's library.

add.tab.fromPlaylist.context: Tab in the add-albums modal. Opens the playlist picker on 07b, then the track list on 07c. Groups an existing playlist's tracks back into the albums they came from.

add.result.meta.context: Second line of a search result row in the add-albums modal.

add.btn.queue.context: Green button on a result row, screen 07, on both the Search Spotify and Saved albums tabs. Puts that album in the Queue on the press — there is no second step to confirm it.

add.chip.added.context: Chip replacing the add button on a result row, screen 07, once that album has been added. It is in the Queue already, so there is nothing left to press.

add.chip.onBoard.context: Chip replacing the add button when the album is already somewhere on the board. {column} is where it is. Prevents the same album occupying two columns. On search results (07) and on playlist track rows (07c), where it replaces the tick.

add.pasteNote.context: Small print under the results, covering the case of finding an album elsewhere and pasting it in.
add.pasteNote.original: Paste a Spotify album link to add directly.
add.pasteNote.translation: Paste a Spotify album link to add directly.

add.foot.count.context: Running count in the add-albums modal footer on the playlist track list, screen 07c — the one tab that picks a batch before writing it. Needs a singular form at n=1. {playlist} is the Queue playlist name.
add.foot.count.original: {n} albums selected · {t} tracks will be appended to {playlist}
add.foot.count.translation: {n} albums selected · {t} tracks will be appended to {playlist}

add.foot.added.context: Running total in the add-albums modal footer, screen 07, on the two tabs where each press writes a record. Past tense: these are already in the playlist. Needs a singular form at n=1. {playlist} is the Queue playlist name.

add.cancel.context: Secondary button in the add-albums modal footer, on the From a playlist tab. Drops what was ticked without writing it.

add.confirm.context: Primary button in the add-albums modal footer, on the From a playlist tab, screens 07b and 07c. Writes the ticked albums.

add.done.context: Primary button in the add-albums modal footer, screen 07, on the Search Spotify and Saved albums tabs. Only closes the modal: each record went in when its own button was pressed.

add.foot.empty.context: Add-albums modal footer before anything is selected, in place of add.foot.count. Screen 07b, where there is nothing to select yet.

add.playlist.filter.context: Placeholder in the search field on the From a playlist tab, screen 07b. Filters the listener's own playlists by name rather than searching Spotify.

add.playlist.meta.context: Second line of a playlist row, screen 07b. {owner} is the playlist owner, add.playlist.owner.you when it's the listener. Counts tracks, not albums — /me/playlists doesn't report albums and working them out would mean reading every playlist first.

add.playlist.owner.you.context: Substituted into {owner} in add.playlist.meta and add.tracks.meta when the listener owns the playlist. Shared playlists read 'You and {n} others'.

add.playlist.owner.shared.context: Substituted into {owner} when the listener owns a collaborative playlist. {n} is the number of other collaborators.

add.playlist.browse.context: Button on a playlist row, screen 07b. Opens that playlist's tracks on 07c. Not 'Add' — nothing is added until tracks are ticked.

add.playlist.chip.unavailable.context: Chip on a dimmed playlist row, screen 07b. Spotify's own algorithmic and editorial playlists — Discover Weekly, Release Radar, the Daily Mixes — return 404 from /playlists/{id}/tracks for apps registered after 27 November 2024. Shown rather than hidden, because an unexplained absence reads as a missing feature.

add.playlist.boardHidden.context: Small print under the playlist list, screen 07b. The seven board playlists are filtered out; browsing the board back into the board would resolve every track to an album already on it.
add.playlist.boardHidden.original: Your seven Gauntlet playlists aren't listed.
add.playlist.boardHidden.translation: Your seven Gauntlet playlists aren't listed.

add.tracks.meta.context: Second line of the header naming the playlist being browsed, screen 07c. {owner} as in add.playlist.meta. The album count is provisional while paging — it counts what has been read, not what the playlist holds.

add.tracks.changePlaylist.context: Button in the playlist header, screen 07c. Returns to the playlist picker on 07b.

add.tracks.hint.context: One line above the track list, screen 07c. States the thing the screen has to make legible: the tick is on a track but the unit of selection is the album, and what gets written is the album's own tracklist rather than the playlist's copy of it.
add.tracks.hint.original: Ticking a track adds the album it came from — every track, in album order.
add.tracks.hint.translation: Ticking a track adds the album it came from — every track, in album order.

add.tracks.selectAll.context: Select-all checkbox above the track list, screen 07c. {n} counts addable albums, so it excludes rows that are already on the board or can't resolve to an album. The whole-playlist case.

add.tracks.clear.context: Button beside the select-all checkbox, screen 07c. Deselects everything.

add.tracks.sub.context: Second line of a track row, screen 07c. {album} is emphasised because it, not the track, is what gets added.

add.tracks.count.context: Right-hand side of an unticked track row, screen 07c. The album's own track count — what ticking the row would add.

add.tracks.willAdd.context: Replaces add.tracks.count once a row is ticked, screen 07c. The plus marks the tracks as being added rather than merely counted.

add.tracks.chip.sameAlbum.context: Chip on a track row whose album another ticked row already selected, screen 07c. The row is ticked but not by itself, so it reads as a consequence rather than a second choice.

add.tracks.chip.single.context: Chip on a dimmed track row, screen 07c. album_type: single, which takes most EPs with it — Spotify types them that way. Unresolvable rows keep their place and say why, because a playlist is a list the listener can already see in Spotify.

add.tracks.chip.compilation.context: Chip on a dimmed track row, screen 07c. album_type: compilation, dropped for the reason First records drops it — five passes through a best-of isn't the exercise.

add.tracks.chip.localFile.context: Chip on a dimmed track row, screen 07c. is_local with a null id, so there's no album to look up.

add.tracks.chip.episode.context: Chip on a dimmed track row, screen 07c. Playlists can hold podcast episodes; they aren't music and have no album.

add.tracks.localSub.context: Replaces add.tracks.sub on a local-file row, screen 07c, which has no artist or album to name.
add.tracks.localSub.original: Added by you · not on Spotify
add.tracks.localSub.translation: Added by you · not on Spotify

narrow.band.inProgress.note.context: Lighter text after the In progress band label on the narrow board, screen 08, where four columns are merged into one.

narrow.column.inProgress.name.context: Heading of the merged middle column on the narrow board.

narrow.column.inProgress.sub.context: Sub-line under the merged column heading. States the sort rule explicitly, since merging four columns costs the spatial ordering.

narrow.card.toDone.withPass.context: Longer variant used when a pass is underway. {p} is which pass, {done}/{total} its progress.

narrow.card.playing.context: Progress label on the narrow-board card currently playing.

narrow.abandoned.summary.context: Collapsed disclosure at the bottom of the Done column on the narrow board, where Abandoned has no column of its own. {n} is the count.

settings.account.head.context: Heading of the first panel on Settings.

settings.account.meta.context: Grey line under the account name on Settings. {tier} is Premium or Free, {time} is how long ago the board last read from Spotify.

settings.reconnect.context: Button on the account row, for re-running the OAuth handshake if the session has gone stale.

settings.playlists.head.context: Section heading above the list of seven playlists on Settings.

settings.playlist.counts.context: Chip on each playlist row on Settings. {a} albums, {t} tracks.

settings.playlist.empty.context: What the playlist count chip shows when a column has nothing in it.

settings.playlist.open.context: Link at the right of each playlist row on Settings. Opens that playlist in Spotify.

settings.rescan.context: Button in the playlist panel footer on Settings. Re-reads the seven playlists, picking up edits made in the Spotify app.

settings.appearance.head.context: Section heading above the theme control on Settings.

settings.appearance.label.context: Row label on the theme control on Settings, and the accessible name of the three-way choice itself.

settings.appearance.hint.context: Grey line under the theme row label on Settings, saying where the choice is kept. There is no database, so it is this browser or nothing.
settings.appearance.hint.original: System follows the device. Anything else is remembered in this browser.
settings.appearance.hint.translation: System follows the device. Anything else is remembered in this browser.

settings.appearance.system.context: First of the three theme choices on Settings. Follows the light-or-dark preference the operating system reports, and is the default.

settings.appearance.light.context: Second of the three theme choices on Settings.

settings.appearance.dark.context: Third of the three theme choices on Settings.

settings.disconnect.head.context: Section heading for the last panel on Settings.

settings.disconnect.label.context: Row label on the disconnect action.

settings.deletePlaylists.label.context: Row label on the destructive delete action, the last thing on Settings.

settings.backLink.context: Link at the very bottom of the Settings page.

login.githubLink.context: Link on the login screen where the invitation-only / open-source paragraph used to be. The five-listener cap is no longer explained in the UI; the repo covers it.

board.loading.context: Shown under the spinner while the board is being read. Everything is derived from Spotify at read time, so a large library is a real wait; saying what is happening beats an unexplained spinner.
